summary:
The Swanson and Hugh Butler Reservoirs Land Conveyances Act authorizes the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Commissioner of Reclamation, to convey certain federal land at Swanson Reservoir and Hugh Butler Reservoir in Nebraska to Hitchcock County and Frontier County. The Act establishes a framework requiring the Secretary to make good faith efforts to negotiate and enter into title transfer agreements with each county within three years of enactment (December 23, 2024).

Section 2 defines key terms, including the five parcels constituting “requested Federal land”: Lakeview Lodge Permitted Concession Land, Red Willow Permitted Cabin Land, Red Willow Permitted Concession Land, Swanson Permitted Cabin Land, and Swanson Permitted Concession Land. The definitions cross-reference specific Bureau of Reclamation maps dated August 2023 and March 2024.

Section 3(a) prescribes the terms of conveyance. Title transfer agreements must provide for conveyance of the applicable parcel in whole, without subdivision, and include a plan demonstrating the county's technical and financial capability to permanently operate and maintain the land and to address state fire, safety, and health codes within two years post-conveyance. The Secretary must negotiate these agreements in accordance with subtitle A of title VIII of the John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act (43 U.S.C. 2901 et seq.), notwithstanding 43 U.S.C. 2902(3)(B). Consideration is fair market value determined by a third-party appraisal conducted under the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice, excluding permit-holder improvements and accounting for future income streams from water service contracts, new contracts, irrigation aid, and other authorized sources. Appraisal disputes are resolved under 43 C.F.R. § 2201.4. Amounts paid are available to the Secretary, subject to further appropriation, for operations at the reservoirs. Conveyance costs are borne by the county in advance. Post-conveyance management must be for substantially the same purposes, or for recreation and public purposes consistent with the Recreation and Public Purposes Act (43 U.S.C. 869 et seq.), public access, fish and wildlife habitat, or preservation of natural character. Section 3(b) prohibits subsequent reconveyance except, under specified conditions, to certain publicly owned or governmental entities within the State, at no cost, and subject to continuing the same management purposes and public access.

Section 4 subjects conveyances to valid existing rights, Pick-Sloan Missouri River Basin Program operational requirements, flowage easements, reservations in the named management agreements, mineral rights and rights-of-way of record as of the date of enactment, deed restrictions prohibiting new permanent structures below specified elevations, and easements for access and improvements. The United States is not liable for flood damage or acts or omissions of permit holders or the counties, except for pre-enactment acts or omissions of the United States. The counties (and any subsequent governmental transferee) must indemnify and hold harmless the United States for claims arising from dam and reservoir operations, survey and conveyance processes, or flood-related damage. Temporary flooding or flood damage is not a taking, and nothing in the Act increases federal tort liability beyond chapter 171 of title 28.

Section 5 provides that the Lakeview Lodge, Red Willow, and Swanson Management Agreements and applicable permits remain in force and effect for the period beginning on enactment and ending on the later of three years post-enactment or the conveyance date. If a title transfer agreement is not entered into by the three-year deadline, the Secretary shall manage the unconveyed land according to applicable law.
